operations.evidence: Fire-safety instructions are required for residents of multi-occupied residential buildings with at least two domestic premises and common parts.
The fact sheet does not determine whether a specific property falls within the legal definition.
Responsible persons should provide instructions in a form residents can reasonably be expected to understand.
A chosen format does not prove comprehension by every resident.
Resident instructions must explain how to report a fire.
The generic duty does not replace building-specific emergency contact and alarm arrangements.
Instructions must remind residents of the building's evacuation strategy.
The reminder does not establish that the strategy is suitable or current.
Instructions must state what residents should do after a fire occurs, based on the building's evacuation strategy.
The requirement does not create a universal action applicable to every building.
Fire-safety instructions should be displayed clearly in communal or conspicuous areas.
Displaying a notice does not prove that residents or visitors read or understood it.
Instructions should be shared directly with residents when they move into the building.
A move-in process record does not prove successful delivery to every occupant.
When the instruction document is updated, it should be displayed again and re-provided to residents.
Redistribution does not establish that the underlying evacuation strategy was properly reviewed.
Fire-safety instructions must be re-provided to residents annually.
Annual provision does not substitute for prompt communication of material changes.
Purpose-built blocks commonly use stay-put or simultaneous evacuation strategies.
These examples must not be assigned to a building without building-specific evidence.
Instructions should reflect the nature of the building and knowledge of its occupants.
General demographic assumptions must not replace evidence about actual resident needs.
Annual and change-triggered provision is intended to keep current fire instructions in residents' minds.
The intended purpose is not proof that the communication changed behaviour or reduced risk.
The regulations do not require translation into multiple languages, although responsible persons may choose to provide translations.
The absence of a translation mandate does not remove the duty to take reasonable steps for understandable communication.
Pictorial information may be used to help residents understand fire-safety instructions.
Pictures alone may be insufficient for complex or individual accessibility needs.
Face-to-face engagement may be used as part of reasonable steps to support resident understanding.
An engagement event does not prove attendance or understanding by all residents.
Responsible persons for existing high-rise residential buildings must provide the local fire and rescue service with information on external-wall design and materials.
A submitted description does not independently verify the actual wall system.
Material changes to a high-rise building's external walls must be notified to the local fire and rescue service.
A notification duty does not establish whether a change is material or has occurred.
The responsible person must provide information on external-fire-spread risk and mitigating steps.
A stated mitigation does not prove implementation or effectiveness.
Where complete wall information is unavailable, responsible persons should provide what they hold, update the fire-risk assessment and send updated information as soon as possible.
Providing partial information does not satisfy missing evidence or prove the assessment is complete.
High-rise responsible persons must prepare and electronically share up-to-date floor plans showing key firefighting equipment for each floor.
Plan submission does not prove accuracy or current site configuration.
Where floors are identical, one floor plan may represent those identical floors.
Visual similarity alone is insufficient to establish that floors are identical.
A single-page building plan should show key firefighting equipment and provide an overview of the building, access points and environs.
A simplified plan does not replace detailed floor plans or operational verification.
Hard copies of floor plans and the building plan should be kept in the secure information box on the premises.
Presence in a box does not prove plans are current, legible or accessible during an incident.
High-rise responsible persons must carry out monthly checks of firefighter lifts, evacuation lifts and relevant control mechanisms.
A monthly check record does not prove the lift will operate in an emergency.
Essential firefighting equipment listed by the regulations requires monthly checking and necessary steps to remedy faults.
A visual or functional check does not replace planned specialist maintenance.
A relevant lift or equipment fault that cannot be resolved within 24 hours must be reported electronically to the fire and rescue service as soon as practicable, with resolution later reported.
The reporting rule does not establish whether a particular defect met the threshold or deadline.
Monthly check outcomes must be recorded openly and made accessible to residents.
Public availability does not prove completeness, accuracy or timely remediation.
Existing high-rise residential buildings must have clear wayfinding markings identifying floors and individual flats.
A signage requirement does not establish that installed signs meet visibility and location specifications.
Wayfinding signage is intended to be visible in normal, low-light and smoky conditions to support firefighter navigation.
Intended visibility must not be assumed without inspection under relevant conditions.
A high-rise building's secure information box should hold responsible-person contact details and hard-copy plans and be accessible to the fire and rescue service.
A box's presence does not prove security, completeness, current contents or operational access.
60 source rows and 124 operation rows were prepared for line-by-line website visibility.
No second runner, queue replacement, runtime execution or business-data write was performed.
